A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hybrid Preferences study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original preference annotations, PPM evaluations, reward-model experiments, Best-of-N and DPO results, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds cross-validation, candidate-pool sensitivity results, and experiments with additional reward-model backbones.

M1.justification: v4 Section 2.4 adds a single-instance routing option: select humans when predicted gain exceeds zero, otherwise select the LM. v3 already used this gain for analysis and budgeted top-k selection, but lacked this threshold rule. The core PPM and simulation-based routing procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: MULTIPREF, Helpsteer2, AlpacaFarm, ChatArena, and appendix Helpsteer2-Preferences coverage are retained, together with the same RewardBench, Best-of-N, and DPO tasks. The additional backbone and candidate-count experiments change settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Human-only, synthetic-only, random-mixture, regressor, top-k versus simulated-routing, and DPO base-SFT comparisons are retained. The new backbone experiments use the existing human-only and synthetic-only annotation baselines.

E3.justification: PPM validation changes from 200 training candidates and 16 held-out candidates to 10-fold cross-validation over 250 candidates, with 225 training and 25 validation candidates per fold. v4 also introduces Helpsteer2 experiments using Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B, and tests candidate pools from 128 to 4096. Standard routing still uses 500 candidates.

E4.justification: v4 adds a focused sensitivity study of simulated candidate-pool size and checks whether selected preference mixtures transfer across reward-model backbones. Existing tag-gain analyses, routing-strategy comparisons, and Helpsteer2 disagreement case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 introduces fold-averaged PPM metrics with ± uncertainty terms, replacing single held-out estimates. The meaning of the ± terms is not explicitly defined. Existing three-run averaging for reward-model comparisons remains unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports hybrid RewardBench scores of 72.4 for both added backbones, versus human-only scores of 64.7 and 71.8. Table 2 replaces quadratic PPM correlation/RMSE of 0.673/0.201 with 0.610/0.266 under the different cross-validation protocol; candidate-pool results are also added. Prior benchmark tables remain unchanged. The Materials Science gain changes from -0.09 to -0.00 in the main summary, conflicting with the retained full appendix value.

T1.justification: Section 5 newly states linear annotation gains, independent samples, and adequate PPM fit as assumptions underlying the gain analysis. The optimization objective and gain definition are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v4 extends the generalization claim to other reward-model backbones. It also strengthens performance summaries to 7–13% over either annotation source and 2–3% Best-of-N gains; v3 tied 7–13% to original datasets and reported up to 3%. Retained Tables 3 and 5 do not support the stronger ranges uniformly.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies the gain analysis by acknowledging that linearity and independence may fail, and adds a limitation concerning variability among human annotators and LMs. It also interprets the new backbone results as evidence of model-agnostic routing. Earlier dataset-quality, scaling, and downstream-policy limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 discloses annotator pay, specifies 7,531 eligible non-tie instances, documents AlpacaFarm instruction/input concatenation, and states that models are released. However, its MULTIPREF prompt omits input/output formatting and decision instructions present in v3 Appendix D.2. Existing reward-model hyperparameters and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Qwen2 technical report and Qwen2.5 references and removes the LMSYS-Chat-1M reference. The substantive positioning relative to active learning, CoAnnotating, datamodels, and data-mixture prediction is retained when related work moves to Appendix A.

P1.justification: v4 introduces the HYPER name throughout, rewrites substantial portions of the abstract and methodology, and creates a separate single-instance routing subsection. Related work and dataset descriptions move to appendices, appendix ordering changes extensively, and the standalone reproducibility statement is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to predominantly two-column layout, with extensively rearranged tables and figures. The PPM scatterplot is replaced by a sensitivity curve, a backbone-results table is added, and the gain-distribution figure moves to the appendix. Existing prompt and case-study boxes become numbered figures, while the main tag summary contracts from ten to five entries per side.

improvement.justification: Cross-validation reduces dependence on v3's small held-out PPM check, while the backbone and candidate-pool experiments provide additional validation. Together with clearer analytical limitations, this modestly strengthens the evidence. Benefits are tempered by overstated performance summaries—Table 5 still shows only 52.8 versus 52.6 for Helpsteer2 hybrid versus human-only—the inconsistent tag-gain summary, and the shortened MULTIPREF prompt.
